svg.aria-label: How to write á é í ó ú: 5 letters, á, é, í, ó, ú, one after another
svg.title: Writing á é í ó ú
svg.desc: 5 letters written one after another: á, é, í, ó, ú (latin). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/LatinPrint-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: á: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class á: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the a after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/a (commit f6dbd80) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>; é: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class é: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e (commit f6dbd80) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>; í: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class í: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the i after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/i (commit f6dbd80) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>; ó: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class ó: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the o after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/o (commit f6dbd80) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>; ú: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class ú: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the u after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/u (commit f6dbd80) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>. Source notes on variation: á: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of á, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are two strokes; the accent is found as a separate mark above the letter in all 120 and drawn last in all 120. Its direction splits: 74 draw it up to the right, 40 down to the left. The a is the Grundschrift-App's a (level kleinbuchstaben/a, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only). The accent is drawn up to the right, as most of these writers draw it; about three in ten draw it down to the left. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the á of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. é: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of é, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are two strokes; the accent is found as a separate mark above the letter in all 120 and drawn last in all 120. Its direction splits: 75 draw it up to the right, 35 down to the left. The e is the Grundschrift-App's e (level kleinbuchstaben/e, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only). The accent is drawn up to the right, as most of these writers draw it; about three in ten draw it down to the left. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the é of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. í: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of í, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 117 are two strokes, because the accent takes the place of the dot. It is found as a separate mark in 69 of the 120 and drawn last in 66 of those 69; 44 of the 69 draw it up to the right, 16 down to the left. The i is the Grundschrift-App's i (level kleinbuchstaben/i, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), with the acute in place of the dot. The accent is drawn up to the right, as most of these writers draw it; about three in ten draw it down to the left. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the í of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. ó: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of ó, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 119 of the 120 are two strokes. The accent is found as a separate mark above the letter in 114 of the 120 and drawn last in all 114. Its direction splits: 74 draw it up to the right, 33 down to the left. The o is the Grundschrift-App's o (level kleinbuchstaben/o, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only). The accent is drawn up to the right, as most of these writers draw it; about three in ten draw it down to the left. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the ó of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. ú: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of ú, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 119 of the 120 are two strokes. The accent is found as a separate mark above the letter in 115 of the 120 and drawn last in all 115. Its direction splits: 70 draw it up to the right, 32 down to the left. The u is the Grundschrift-App's u (level kleinbuchstaben/u, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only). The accent is drawn up to the right, as most of these writers draw it; about three in ten draw it down to the left. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the ú of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 2 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 5 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class á: 120 tablet pen traces by
60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the a after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/a (commit f6dbd80)
Letter 2: stroke order after UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class é: 120 tablet pen traces by
60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e (commit f6dbd80)
Letter 3: stroke order after UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class í: 120 tablet pen traces by
60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the i after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/i (commit f6dbd80)
Letter 4: stroke order after UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class ó: 120 tablet pen traces by
60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the o after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/o (commit f6dbd80)
Letter 5: stroke order after UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class ú: 120 tablet pen traces by
60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the u after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/u (commit f6dbd80)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
